VERIDANE - INTERNAL - Product Safety Committee memo PSC-2026-07
Date: 2 Oct 2026     From: Elena Kowalczyk, VP Quality & Product Safety     To: Executive Leadership Team

Subject: GV-400 series combination gas valve - voluntary recall (CPSC Fast Track)

Summary
- Affected units: ~41,200 GV-400/GV-410 combination gas valves, date codes 2507-2612, sold to OEMs for commercial rooftop units and unit heaters.
- Issue: diaphragm seat can deform under sustained high-inlet-pressure conditions, allowing gas to pass when the valve is commanded closed. 17 field reports of gas odor; 2 reports of delayed ignition causing cabinet damage; no injuries reported.
- Root cause: change of diaphragm compound supplier (Q1 2025); supplier lot material out of spec on compression set. Corrective action complete; replacement valves shipping from Mequon plant since 28 Sep.
- Regulatory: CPSC Fast Track filed 22 Sep; joint recall notice expected the week of 19 Oct. Canada (Health Canada) notification filed.
- Cost: reserve booked in Q3 $21.6M (field replacement, OEM labour reimbursement, logistics). Range $18-26M. Supplier recovery claim of ~$9M lodged, not recognised.
- Customer impact: three OEMs (incl. our 2nd-largest BCV customer) have paused new GV-400 orders pending the recall notice. Included in updated guidance.

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

The growth engine of this company accelerated in the third quarter. Thermal & Data Center Solutions net sales rose 13.4% to $156.3 million, we won two new hyperscale awards, and our data-center cooling backlog reached a record $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year. Total backlog climbed 13.0% to a record $918.0 million. That is the clearest signal we can give you about demand for the products that will define Veridane's next several years.

At the same time, our core commercial HVAC business stayed soft, and we moved quickly and deliberately on a voluntary product recall in our gas valve line. We are updating our full-year outlook to reflect those realities, and we are acting on cost with a program we believe changes the earnings power of the business.

## Highlights

- Thermal & Data Center Solutions net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million; data-center cooling backlog of $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year.
- Total backlog up 13.0% to a record $918.0 million.

- Completed a voluntary, proactive recall of the GV-400 series gas valve under the CPSC Fast Track program, with root cause corrected and replacement valves shipping since 28 September.

GAAP results for the quarter — including the recall charge and Keystone restructuring costs — are provided in the accompanying KPI tables and in our Form 10-Q.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions.** Net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4%, on continued demand for precision cooling across hyperscale and colocation customers. We were awarded two new hyperscale programs in the quarter, and the CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger is ramping with hyperscale customers following its Q2 launch. Segment backlog ended the quarter at $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year, and now represents well over half of company backlog. Liquid cooling is a natural extension of the fluid-handling expertise this company has built over four decades, and it is where our capital is going.

**Building Controls & Valves.** Net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9%, reflecting the softer commercial construction activity we flagged in prior quarters and a slower pace of equipment replacement. In September we initiated a voluntary recall of approximately 41,200 GV-400 and GV-410 combination gas valves, working with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission under its Fast Track program and notifying Health Canada. The root cause — a supplier lot of the diaphragm compound that was out of specification — has been corrected, and replacement valves have been shipping from our Mequon plant since 28 September. We recorded a $21.6 million reserve in the quarter for field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement and logistics. We acted quickly and put customers first, and we are working closely with our OEM partners as the recall notice is published. Three OEM customers, including our second-largest BCV customer, have paused new GV-400 orders pending publication of the recall notice, which is reflected in our updated outlook. BCV backlog was essentially flat at $343.8 million, up 0.6% year over year.

## Outlook

We are updating our full-year FY2026 guidance to net sales of $1.66–1.70 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $205–215 million, from $1.78–1.84 billion and $255–270 million previously. The strength of the data-center franchise is unchanged and building: the backlog that feeds FY2027 revenue grew 22.0% in the quarter.

Keystone is sized against a cost base built for a larger commercial HVAC business than the one we expect in the near term, and we intend to hold those savings as volume returns.

We are managing the business for cash: tight receivables and inventory discipline and deliberate phasing of capital spending. Capital expenditures were $14.9 million in the quarter and $41.8 million year to date, weighted toward capacity that serves the data-center franchise. We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash. Further detail on our financial position will be included in our Form 10-Q.

The third quarter asked a great deal of our people — a product recall executed at speed, a cost program launched, and a growth franchise that kept accelerating. We are grateful to the 6,200 employees of Veridane, to the OEM and hyperscale customers who continue to place their programs with us, and to you, our shareholders, for your continued confidence.

We will host our earnings call on Thursday, 5 November 2026 at 4:30 p.m. ET.

# Veridane Fluid Technologies, Inc. (NASDAQ: VRDF) — Q3 FY2026 Letter to Shareholders

**DRAFT — FOR REVIEW BY D. WHITCOMBE / M. OSTRANDER / P. RAMAN — NOT FOR RELEASE**
Ticket IR-2026-Q3-014 | Draft 1 | Prepared for release with Q3 FY2026 results, Thursday 5 November 2026, 4:05 pm ET
All figures per the controller package (q3_financials.md v3), unaudited. $M with one decimal; percentages with one decimal.

---

Dear Fellow Shareholders,

The growth engine of this company accelerated in the third quarter. Thermal & Data Center Solutions net sales rose 13.4% to $156.3 million, we won two new hyperscale awards, and our data-center cooling backlog reached a record $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year. Total backlog climbed 13.0% to a record $918.0 million. That is the clearest signal we can give you about demand for the products that will define Veridane's next several years.

At the same time, our core commercial HVAC business stayed soft, and we moved quickly and deliberately on a voluntary product recall in our gas valve line. We are updating our full-year outlook to reflect those realities, and we are acting on cost with a program we believe changes the earnings power of the business.

## Highlights

- Thermal & Data Center Solutions net sales up 13.4% to $156.3 million; data-center cooling backlog of $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year.
- Total backlog up 13.0% to a record $918.0 million.
- Two new hyperscale awards won in the quarter, extending the momentum behind the CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger launched in Q2.
- Adjusted EBITDA of $48.7 million, an 11.8% margin; adjusted EPS of $0.15.
- Launched Project Keystone, a structural cost and footprint program targeting $35 million of run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027.
- Completed a voluntary, proactive recall of the GV-400 series gas valve under the CPSC Fast Track program, with root cause corrected and replacement valves shipping since 28 September.

GAAP results for the quarter — including the recall charge and Keystone restructuring costs — are provided in the accompanying KPI tables and in our Form 10-Q.

## Segment review

**Thermal & Data Center Solutions.** Net sales were $156.3 million, up 13.4%, on continued demand for precision cooling across hyperscale and colocation customers. We were awarded two new hyperscale programs in the quarter, and the CR-9 rear-door heat exchanger is ramping with hyperscale customers following its Q2 launch. Segment backlog ended the quarter at $574.2 million, up 22.0% year over year, and now represents well over half of company backlog. Liquid cooling is a natural extension of the fluid-handling expertise this company has built over four decades, and it is where our capital is going. We are adding capacity at the plants that serve these programs, and supply chain and labor are the constraints we manage hardest to protect the delivery schedules in that backlog.

**Building Controls & Valves.** Net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9%, reflecting the softer commercial construction activity we flagged in prior quarters and a slower pace of equipment replacement. In September we initiated a voluntary recall of approximately 41,200 GV-400 and GV-410 combination gas valves, working with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission under its Fast Track program and notifying Health Canada. The root cause — a supplier lot of the diaphragm compound that was out of specification — has been corrected, and replacement valves have been shipping from our Mequon plant since 28 September. We recorded a $21.6 million reserve in the quarter for field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement and logistics. We acted quickly and put customers first, and we are working closely with our OEM partners as the recall notice is published. Three OEM customers, including our second-largest BCV customer, have paused new GV-400 orders pending publication of the recall notice, which is reflected in our updated outlook. BCV backlog was essentially flat at $343.8 million, up 0.6% year over year.

## Outlook

We are updating our full-year FY2026 guidance to net sales of $1.66–1.70 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $205–215 million, from $1.78–1.84 billion and $255–270 million previously. The change is driven by the continued softness in commercial HVAC and gas valves, including the paused GV-400 orders, and by the cost of the recall. The strength of the data-center franchise is unchanged and building: the backlog that feeds FY2027 revenue grew 22.0% in the quarter.

Project Keystone is the program we are most focused on. It targets $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027, through footprint consolidation, sourcing and supply-chain actions, and simplification of the BCV product line. We recorded $6.2 million of restructuring charges in the quarter ($9.8 million year to date). Keystone is sized against a cost base built for a larger commercial HVAC business than the one we expect in the near term, and we intend to hold those savings as volume returns.

We are managing the business for cash. Free cash flow was negative $11.3 million in the quarter and negative $4.2 million year to date, reflecting recall and Keystone outflows alongside capital spending of $14.9 million in the quarter and $41.8 million year to date, weighted toward capacity that serves the data-center franchise. As the recall program winds down and Keystone savings come through, we expect working capital to become a source of cash as those shipments ramp. We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash. Further detail on our financial position will be included in our Form 10-Q.

## Closing

The third quarter asked a great deal of our people — a product recall executed at speed, a cost program launched, and a growth franchise that kept accelerating. We are grateful to the 6,200 employees of Veridane, to the OEM and hyperscale customers who continue to place their programs with us, and to you, our shareholders, for your continued confidence.

We will host our earnings call on Thursday, 5 November 2026 at 4:30 p.m. ET.

Sincerely,

**Dana Whitcombe**
President & Chief Executive Officer

**Mark Ostrander**
EVP & Chief Financial Officer

Liquid cooling is a natural extension of the fluid-handling expertise that has always defined this company, and it is where our capital is going. We are adding capacity at the plants that serve these programs, and supply chain and labor are the constraints we manage hardest to protect the delivery schedules in that backlog.

**Building Controls & Valves.** Net sales were $256.3 million, down 14.9%, reflecting the softer commercial construction activity we flagged in prior quarters. In September we initiated a voluntary recall of approximately 41,200 GV-400 and GV-410 combination gas valves, working with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission under its Fast Track program and notifying Health Canada. The root cause — a supplier lot of the diaphragm compound that was out of specification — has been corrected, and replacement valves have been shipping from our Mequon plant since 28 September. We recorded a $21.6 million reserve in the quarter for field replacement, OEM labor reimbursement and logistics. We acted quickly and put customers first, and we are working closely with our OEM partners as the recall notice is published. Three OEM customers, including our second-largest BCV customer, have paused new GV-400 orders pending publication of the recall notice, which is reflected in our updated outlook. BCV backlog was essentially flat at $343.8 million, up 0.6% year over year.

## Outlook

We are updating our full-year FY2026 guidance to net sales of $1.66–1.70 billion and adjusted EBITDA of $205–215 million, from $1.78–1.84 billion and $255–270 million previously. The change is driven by the continued softness in commercial HVAC and gas valves, including the paused GV-400 orders, and by the cost of the recall. The strength of the data-center franchise is unchanged and building: the backlog that feeds FY2027 revenue grew 22.0% in the quarter.

Project Keystone is the program we are most focused on. It targets $35 million of annualized run-rate savings by the end of Q2 FY2027, through footprint consolidation, sourcing and supply-chain actions, and simplification of the BCV product line. We recorded $6.2 million of restructuring charges in the quarter ($9.8 million year to date). Keystone is sized against a cost base built for a larger commercial HVAC business than the one we expect in the near term, and we intend to hold those savings as volume returns.

We are managing the business for cash. Free cash flow was negative $11.3 million in the quarter and negative $4.2 million year to date, reflecting recall and Keystone outflows alongside capital spending of $14.9 million in the quarter and $41.8 million year to date, weighted toward capacity that serves the data-center franchise. As the recall program winds down and Keystone savings come through, we expect working capital to become a source of cash as those shipments ramp. We ended the quarter with $96.4 million of cash. Further detail on our financial position will be included in our Form 10-Q.

## Closing

The third quarter asked a great deal of our people — a product recall executed at speed, a cost program launched, and a growth franchise that kept accelerating. We are grateful to the 6,200 employees of Veridane, to the OEM and hyperscale customers who continue to place their programs with us, and to you, our shareholders, for your continued confidence.

We will host our earnings call on Thursday, 5 November 2026 at 4:30 p.m. ET.

Sincerely,

**Dana Whitcombe**
